evidence.claim: highlighting rugged canyons, redwoods and Pacific coastal views.

evidence.claim: The Big Sur coast section became California’s first State Scenic Highway in 1965.
evidence.quote: The section of road along the Big Sur Coast was declared the first State Scenic Highway in 1965

evidence.claim: California approved the Carmel–San Simeon Highway in 1919 to connect Big Sur with the rest of the state.
evidence.quote: The state first approved building Route 56, or the Carmel-San Simeon Highway, to connect Big Sur to the rest of California in 1919.

evidence.claim: San Quentin State Prison established three temporary camps whose inmates supplied construction labor.
evidence.quote: San Quentin State Prison set up three temporary prison camps to provide unskilled convict labor to help with road construction.

evidence.claim: The route required 33 bridges, with Bixby the largest.
evidence.quote: The route necessitated construction of 33 bridges, the largest of which was the Bixby Bridge.

evidence.claim: New Deal funds helped finish the work during the Depression, and the paved two-lane road opened on June 17, 1937, after eighteen years of construction.
evidence.quote: After 18 years of construction, aided by New Deal funds during the Great Depression, the paved two-lane road was completed and opened on June 17, 1937.

evidence.claim: Landslides have repeatedly interrupted this coastal connection, including a 2011 slide that closed the highway for months.
evidence.quote: A March 2011 landslide in the Big Sur region forced Caltrans to close the highway for several months.

evidence.claim: Traveling south, Carmel Highlands forms the northern gateway to the Big Sur coast.
evidence.quote: Carmel Highlands is just south of the Point Lobos State Reserve, and serves as the northern gateway of the Big Sur coastline along California State Route 1.

evidence.claim: Bixby Creek Bridge comes before Point Sur and the Big Sur River valley.
evidence.quote: The Old Coast Road from the north side of Bixby Creek is 11 miles (18 km) long, cutting inland across the Little Sur River, and ends near the northern border of Andrew Molera State Park, 8.3 miles (13.4 km) to the south along Highway 1.

evidence.claim: Bixby Creek Bridge comes before Point Sur and the Big Sur River valley.

evidence.claim: San Carpóforo Creek flows through its canyon into a small Pacific bay and is generally considered the southern boundary of the Big Sur region.
evidence.quote: San Carpóforo Creek flows through San Carpóforo Canyon and into the Pacific Ocean in a small bay 20 miles (32 km) north of San Simeon on the Central Coast of California. The creek is generally considered to be the southern border of the Big Sur region of Central California.

evidence.claim: The Big Sur Chamber of Commerce reported Highway 1 fully open through Big Sur on September 14, 2026.
evidence.quote: Highway One Closure Update September 14, 2026 Highway One is now fully open through Big Sur.

evidence.claim: Bixby’s concrete arch replaced a long diversion inland.
evidence.quote: At Bixby Creek, the road was necessarily built 11 miles (18 km) inland to circumvent the deep canyon.

evidence.claim: Before the bridge opened in 1932, the Old Coast Road went eleven miles inland and became impassable in winter.
evidence.quote: Before the opening of the bridge in 1932, residents of the Big Sur area were virtually cut off during winter due to blockages on the often impassable Old Coast Road, which led 11 miles (18 km) inland.

evidence.claim: Engineers considered a smaller inland bridge with a tunnel before choosing the coastal crossing.
evidence.quote: State engineers considered two alternatives to crossing the creek, an inland route and a smaller bridge, or a coastal location and a larger bridge. The inland route would have needed an 890-foot (270 m) tunnel

evidence.claim: Concrete reduced construction and maintenance costs and echoed the surrounding rock, part of the reason engineers chose it over steel.
evidence.quote: They chose concrete in part because it would not only reduce both construction and maintenance costs but would also echo the color and composition of the natural rock cliff formations in the area.

evidence.claim: The arch has tall supporting columns above it; the two large vertical buttresses at its sides are decorative rather than structurally necessary.
evidence.quote: The two large, vertical buttresses or supporting pillars on either side of the arch, while aesthetically pleasing, are functionally unnecessary.

evidence.claim: The arch has tall supporting columns above it
evidence.quote: the parabolic shape of the arch, the tall spandrel columns, and the architectural piers

evidence.claim: The bridge was finished five years before the through highway.
evidence.quote: The bridge was completed on October 15, 1932, although the highway was not finished for another five years.

evidence.claim: Point Sur’s lighthouse had a road connection in the making before the coastal highway.
evidence.quote: In 1888, Joseph Post won a government contract to build a road to connect the road his father built and Point Sur,  the future site of the Point Sur Lighthouse.

evidence.claim: In 1888, Joseph Post won a government contract to link his father’s road with Point Sur, the future lighthouse site.
evidence.quote: In 1888, Joseph Post won a government contract to build a road to connect the road his father built and Point Sur,  the future site of the Point Sur Lighthouse.

evidence.claim: The point’s name predates that work: the U.S. Coast Survey named it Point Sur in 1851, describing a point that looked like an island.
evidence.quote: The first American use of the name "Sur" was by the U.S. Coast Survey in 1851, which renamed a point of land that looked like an island and was shaped like a trumpet

evidence.claim: Offshore from nearby Andrew Molera State Park, the Point Sur marine reserve and conservation area protect ocean wildlife and ecosystems.
evidence.quote: Point Sur State Marine Reserve and Marine Conservation Area are marine protected areas offshore from Andrew Molera State Park.  Like underwater parks, these marine protected areas help conserve ocean wildlife and marine ecosystems.
